title: "Guaranteed returns" paid into a personal account vs. mutual-fund discussion with risk disclosure
summary: A caller who says they are the recipient's relationship manager at Kaveri Bank phones about the large idle balance in the recipient's savings account. In the fraud case, the caller pitches an "exclusive scheme" with guaranteed monthly returns and asks the recipient to transfer money to the caller's own UPI ID so they can invest it. In the legitimate case, the manager suggests mutual funds, says returns are market-linked and not guaranteed, and says any investment is made in the recipient's own name through the bank's app or branch forms.

shared_setting.pretext: a savings balance of about [AMOUNT_1] (₹1,00,000–₹10,00,000) earning low interest.
shared_setting.recipient_profile: an adult customer with some savings but little investing experience; profile sampled at generation.
other_facts: Both callers mention percentage returns and say the balance could "work harder".

fraud.label_rationale: The caller asks the recipient to send their money to a personal account for the caller to invest, and promises guaranteed returns. Legitimate investments are made in the investor's own name, and returns in market products cannot be guaranteed.
fraud.caller_objective: Get the recipient to transfer [AMOUNT_2] (₹25,000–₹5,00,000) to [UPI_ID_1].
stable_facts: The caller promises a fixed monthly return, for example "3% every month, guaranteed".
[UPI_ID_1] is described as "my investment desk ID" or "the scheme account".
The caller says the scheme is available only to a few "priority" customers and closes this week.

evidence.text: Caller asks the recipient to transfer money to [UPI_ID_1] so the caller can invest it on their behalf
Caller promises guaranteed or fixed high returns

legitimate.label_rationale: The manager suggests market-linked products with an explicit risk disclosure and routes any investment through official channels in the recipient's own name. No transfer to the caller is asked.
legitimate.caller_objective: Book a meeting or get the recipient to review mutual-fund options in the app.
stable_facts: The manager mentions mutual funds distributed by the bank and past returns, and says past performance does not guarantee future returns.
Any investment is made through the Investments section of the Kaveri Bank app or a signed form at the branch, with units held in the recipient's name.
The manager offers to send the scheme documents through the app's secure inbox and suggests the recipient take time to decide.

caller_continuation_limits: The fraud caller may offer a smaller "trial" transfer, show fake returns, or pressure. They must not switch to a different mechanism (for example app install, OTP, or link). The legitimate caller must not ask for any transfer to themselves, guarantee returns, or request credentials after the branch.

must_preserve: risk disclosure and investment in the recipient's own name (_L)
may_vary: percentages (fictional, not tied to real funds)
up to 2 filler turns before turn 3
must_not_emit: real fund, exchange, or regulator names
real fund returns presented as fact

ambiguities: Percentages and "limited period" can appear in both cases. The legitimate manager may be enthusiastic. The label depends on the transfer to the caller.
A genuine relationship manager may push products hard. Mis-selling is not fraud in this dataset's sense and must not be labelled as such.

Real investment fraud often runs through messaging groups and fake trading apps over weeks. This card keeps one call and the bank pretext. Cross-domain overlap: jr_16 (crypto "job" requiring own investment).
